## On-demand streaming “exerts the greatest volumetric pressure” on internet traffic: Sandvine 

 By CSI

 12/04/2024

Google, Facebook, and Netflix continue to dominate internet traffic, driving nearly 70% of all fixed and mobile data consumption globally, according to Sandvine’s 2024 Global Internet Phenomena Report. The report highlights that global internet traffic has surpassed 33 exabytes per day, with users averaging 4.2GB daily across 6.4 billion mobile and 1.4 billion fixed connections. Key findings include: • Google, Facebook, and Netflix account for 65% of all fixed traffic and 68% of all mobile traffic. • Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Netflix (MAMAAN), TikTok, and Disney+ constitute 65% of total internet volume. • Video content, especially on-demand streaming, dominates downstream traffic, with YouTube leading in both app and subscriber volumes across all regions. average • On-Demand Streaming is the type of video that generates the most traffic, with per-subscriber volume of 7.9 GB per day (54% of total downstream volume). Of that volume, the app that drives the most traffic is YouTube, contributing 1.9 GB per sub, per day, with Netflix in second at 1.4 GB per sub per day • Downstream subscriber volume in fixed networks is 14.5 GB; and 1.2 GB for upstream – much larger than Mobile’s averages of 1.6 GB and 0.1 GB. This indicates people are waiting to watch bigger videos over Wi-Fi, opting to instead do Social Media over mobile devices, while on the move • Social Media is the biggest app category in mobile networks’ downstream traffic, with 35%, and 7 of the top 10 apps attributable to Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, WhatsApp, Telegram, and X. Social Media is also the largest contributor to upstream traffic on mobile, due in large part to the sharing and posting of videos on apps like TikTok and Facebook Messenger. • Despite the volumetric power of Social Media over Mobile, YouTube still comes out on top for overall per-sub volume, with 233 MB per sub, per day. The report also notes the rising trend of file sharing and delivery, driven by automatic phone backups and VPNs, as well as the increasing complexity of applications, blending various content types like video, audio, live streaming, messaging, and gaming.

The latest in the CSI podcast series has Goran Nastic and Harmonic’s Rob Gambino talk through the latest opportunities and innovations around content monetisation. Content monetisation takes many shapes and forms, and while the concept is not new it is a hot topic, with advertising enjoying a resurgence thanks to the growth of FAST and ad-supported hybrid streaming tiers. Rob talks us through various emerging business models and technological advancements taking place in targeted advertising, such as revenue-per-second and ad-pod optimisation, as well as dynamic brand insertion and new ad formats.
